MBA AI & DS · Batch 2025–27 · Term 5

Natural Language Processing

Most of the data a business has is text: reviews, tickets, emails, contracts. Over the course of this term you will learn to turn that text into structure, then into numbers, then into models and products that support decisions.

  • Thursdays 2:30–5:15 pm (break 3:45–4:00)
  • Venue MSIS campus
  • Credits 3 · 24 sessions · 12 workshops
  • Instructor Prof. Shripada Hebbar
Before 1 October

Set up your laptop by following the setup guide, then read the Workshop 1 pre-read. Setup takes about 20 minutes on a good connection.

How each Thursday runs

Each Thursday is one workshop made of two sessions, with a break in the middle. The format is the same every week:

2:30 – 3:45 · First half

Understand it

A business hook, then the idea worked by hand on a tiny example, then a guided notebook where we build the same thing at scale.

3:45 – 4:00

Break

Get some chai, and restart your kernel.

4:00 – 5:15 · Second half

Use it

A challenge lab in pairs, a share-out where we discuss what a manager would do with the result, and a short check at the end.

Every algorithm in this course gets three treatments: by hand (which is what the closed-book exams test), in code (which is what the lab test checks), and as a decision (which is what you will actually use at work).

The running case

We work with one dataset all term: 30,000 real Amazon customer reviews of home appliances and parts (water filters, washer and dryer parts, ice makers, coffee machine accessories), along with metadata for 946 products. Each week adds a new capability to the same data:

clean it with regex → search it → model its language → read its sentiment → turn it into vectors → recommend products → apply transformers.

Source: Amazon Reviews 2023, McAuley Lab, UC San Diego (Hou et al., 2024). We use a subset for teaching. Some workshops add small extra datasets.

Assessment

Component Weight When Format
Lab test 20% After W6 (session 12) Individual. A notebook task followed by a viva. Covers Units 1–2 (CO1).
Mid-term 20% Institute schedule Closed book, 90 minutes. Covers CO2 (Naïve Bayes, TF-IDF, word2vec).
Quiz 10% W11 (after session 21) Individual.
Mini project 10% Assigned W7 · checkpoint W11 · pitch W12 Teams of 3–4. Topics are assigned by lottery. Every project must use at least one technique from each unit.
End-term 40% Institute schedule Closed book, 120 minutes. Covers CO3 (recommender systems and transformer architectures).

Plagiarism policy: a similarity index of up to 10% is permitted. Anything above that falls under section 8.4 of the PGP handbook.
